children: , the advanced-lithography equipment leader, faced a very different AI-chip bottleneck: building EUV machines fast enough to keep pace with demand. U.S. shares gained approximately 1.0% to $1,696.12, extending investor enthusiasm around the company's potential to assemble more than 110 EUV systems in 2028. The valuation picture is already demanding, though. At $1,696.12, ASML trades 33.98% above its GF Value estimate of roughly $1,270, showing how much future execution is already embedded in the stock.

Capacity is now the story. Reuters reported that ASML is nearly sold out for 2027, when manufacturing capacity stands at at least 80 EUV machines. Pushing production beyond 110 systems in 2028 would mean increasing annual output by at least 37.5% from that stated floor. The financial engine gives ASML room to invest: its second-quarter results included 9.33 billion of revenue, a 54% gross margin and 2.92 billion of net income.

The opportunity is huge, but so is the execution test. Every additional EUV machine can unlock more semiconductor-fab capacity for customers chasing advanced AI chips, yet ASML cannot simply push units through the factory faster. These are extraordinarily complex systems, and installation timing, customer acceptance and manufacturing precision all matter. If ASML can move from at least 80 machines toward more than 110 without sacrificing margins or delivery quality, the revenue ceiling rises sharply. With the shares already trading well above GF Value, however, investors are paying for a meaningful chunk of that capacity expansion before it arrives.

title: ASML Adds 1% as 110 EUV Tools Test Factory Throughput
